As far as JD Sports is concerned,

analysts Russ Mould and Danni Hewson said the sportswear retailer recently tripped up, slashing its profit outlook on continued US weakness amid cost-of-living pressures and delayed back to school spending.

"The half-year trading update wasn’t uniformly negative with bright spots in Asia Pacific and the UK which returned to positive like-for-like sales growth in the second quarter, supported by strong sales of football replica kit," they said.

"Despite the profit downgrade JD Sports stuck to its free cash flow guidance with the group flipping into a net cash position in early August from a net debt position. This provides it with some cushioning to absorb the pressure from downbeat consumer sentiment.
"Investors will be looking for clarity on the extent of US promotional activity and margin implications as well as an update on ongoing store closures."

analyst Charlotte de Montpellier said: "Swiss economic growth has recently surprised on the upside, but inflation remains too low to warrant a change in monetary policy. We expect the Swiss National Bank to keep its policy rate at 0% next Thursday and to remain on hold over the coming quarters."
There are no major UK corporate releases due on Friday, but in the US, the Michigan consumer sentiment index for September will be out, along with durable goods orders for August.
